reden: No. The report’s liquidation issue is about a unit mismatch in executeLiquidate: the liquidation reward is computed from futureValue (borrow-token units) and added to collateral-token amounts, resulting in an almost-zero reward. The vulnerability description H-03 concerns a different bug in the same function: the collateral remainder cap is miscomputed using crLiquidation (e.g., 130%) instead of only the excess over 100% (crLiquidation - 100%), causing unfair protocol fee distribution. These have different root causes, affect different lines of logic (reward units vs. remainder cap), require different fixes (unit conversion vs. adjusting the cap formula), and an exploit/fix for one would not address the other.
